headline: Four-week volume is up 16% and easy-run cardiac drift is trending down — aerobic efficiency appears to be improving alongside the load increase.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic base is responding well to a sustained increase in training stimulus. Easy-run heart rate has dropped meaningfully compared to the prior block at comparable efforts, which is a reliable within-athlete signal of improving aerobic efficiency — not just a pace or load artefact. Combined with the volume increase, this suggests your body is adapting rather than merely accumulating fatigue.

The 20-week running streak matching your personal best is worth noting not as a milestone but as structural evidence: consistent, unbroken training across this window is precisely the kind of base that supports both ultra durability and speed ceiling. The threshold data point from earlier this week — a strong effort at a pace well inside your half-marathon PB range — is consistent with this picture.

Strength is slightly lighter this block, which in isolation means little given the volume increase and the overall year-to-date session count. Nothing here suggests a meaningful drop in strength capacity; it reads more like natural load distribution across modalities.
watch_items: Watch whether the downward easy-run HR trend continues as this week's longer run is absorbed — a plateau or reversal would be worth noting.
Monitor how the 16% volume step lands across the next two weeks; back-to-back durability and morning feel are better signals here than any single session.
The threshold data point is new and isolated — watch whether subsequent comparable efforts confirm or revise that benchmark before weighting it heavily.
Keep an eye on strength frequency over the coming weeks; with volume elevated, intentional scheduling of strength sessions matters more, not less.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
